expectations.text: Inputs get associated label elements and appropriate types and autocomplete attributes
expectations.evidence: The Write replaced the divs with <label for="email"> and <label for="password">. The email input became type="email" with name and autocomplete="email". The password input got name and autocomplete="new-password".

expectations.text: The removed focus outline is replaced with a visible focus style, and the div button becomes a real button reachable by Tab
expectations.evidence: The rewrite removed `input:focus { outline: none; }` and added `input:focus-visible, button:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #1a56db; outline-offset: 2px; }`. The `<div class="btn" onclick>` became `<button type="submit">`.

expectations.text: Error messaging uses aria-invalid and aria-describedby (and an announced region where appropriate) with sufficient color contrast
expectations.evidence: The email input has aria-describedby="email-error", and the error span has aria-live="polite". The submit handler sets aria-invalid="true". The error colour changed from #f88 to #b00020, which has high contrast on white.

expectations.text: The findings are listed, and verification with keyboard-only navigation or an accessibility checker is described
expectations.evidence: The final message lists the findings with line references. It says no axe, Lighthouse, browser keyboard pass or screen reader test was run. It does describe a markup-based keyboard check: Tab order is email, password, button, and focus is visible. It does not describe how a keyboard-only or checker verification would be done, but it does address verification. This is a borderline pass.
